changes.title: Sort, filter and download every list
changes.text: Every table and list on the site can now be sorted by clicking a column heading, filtered with a search box (and drop-downs where a column has a few values), and downloaded as a CSV of exactly the rows on screen, in the order shown. Lists open newest first, then A to Z; upcoming meetings open soonest first.

changes.title: An API for BayCounty.me
changes.text: Every dataset on the site is now available through a free, read-only API with filtering, sorting and CSV output, plus an MCP server so AI assistants can look up and cite these records directly.

changes.title: Correction: Money map
changes.text: The first version of the Money map overstated connections. It counted a donor's contracts again for every official the donor gave to, which roughly doubled the government totals, and it drew lines from officials to governments they don't serve on. The map now puts each donor in the middle: campaign gifts on one side, the governments that pay the donor on the other, each counted once. It marks only gifts to an official whose own government pays that donor, and lists the recorded votes those officials cast on that donor's contracts. The heat map that credited contract dollars to individual officials was removed.

changes.title: Who's running in 2026
changes.text: Every local race on Bay County ballots this year, with each candidate's platform in their own words, links to their campaigns, and their campaign money: what they raised and spent, how much came from individuals, organizations and their own pockets, and every business or committee that gave. Races already decided are shown separately.

changes.title: Property tax exemptions, and exemptions on My Address
changes.text: A new page shows every property tax exemption in the 2026 tax roll, from homestead to disabled veterans, with how many homes get each and how much tax it takes off bills. My Address now lists each exemption on a home by name and uses the certified school and non-school taxable values, which corrects estimates for fully exempt homes and for seniors with the county senior exemption.

changes.title: Money map
changes.text: An interactive map of which businesses and groups gave to which officials, and where those same donors hold contracts with a local government, plus heat maps of giving by government and of contract dollars held by each official's donors.

changes.title: Every bond, note and loan
changes.text: The Debt page now lists each of 61 bond, note and loan issues with the amount borrowed, what is still owed, the rate, the final payment date and what it paid for.

changes.title: A page for each government
changes.text: Bay County, the School Board and each of the seven cities now have one page that pulls together who runs it, its budget and property tax rate, debt, audit findings, recorded votes, contracts, projects and upcoming meetings.

changes.title: Compare governments side by side
changes.text: Pick any governments and compare budgets, tax rates, debt and staffing, in total or per resident.

changes.title: Upcoming public meetings
changes.text: Every board's next meetings, with agenda links and the money items on each agenda, checked daily. Add them all to your phone or computer calendar with one link.

changes.title: Campaign money and contracts
changes.text: The most recent campaign of each current elected official: how much they raised, from individuals and organizations, and which donors also hold contracts with local governments. Individual donors are counted, not named; each official's full report is linked.

changes.title: Request a public record
changes.text: Pick a government and a record this site is missing, or describe your own, and get a ready-to-send Florida public records request with the right office's contact details.

changes.title: Open data downloads
changes.text: Every dataset on the site, as CSV and JSON files you can open in a spreadsheet, with a description of each column.

changes.title: Zoning and development near your address
changes.text: My Address now shows the zoning and future land use at the address, development projects and orders within half a mile, recent rezonings, and conditional uses nearby.

changes.title: BayCounty.me en español
changes.text: My Address, the records request tool and the glossary are now available in Spanish. Mi dirección, solicitudes de registros y el glosario, en español.

changes.title: Address lookup understands more ways of typing an address
changes.text: My Address now finds addresses typed with full street types (Drive, Avenue, Boulevard), directions (North, West), highway forms (Hwy 98, US 98, County Road 2321), Saint or St., spelled-out numbers (Tenth Street), MLK, unit numbers, and a city, state and ZIP on the end. If a street type is wrong, it shows the closest matches.

changes.title: Clearer vote summaries
changes.text: Every recorded vote now has a plain-English headline and summary saying what was decided, rewritten from the motion in the minutes. The earlier text was pasted from the minutes and was often hard to read. Each card shows who voted which way and links to the minutes.

changes.title: Correction: flood zones on My Address
changes.text: Flood zones now come live from FEMA's National Flood Hazard Layer, which reflects Bay County's October 24, 2024 flood maps. The earlier lookup used an older county copy that missed high-risk zones for some addresses (about 8% in a sample of 300) and showed outdated base flood elevations. Results now also show the FIRM panel and any map revision, with a link to check the address on FEMA's map. Thanks to the readers who reported it.

changes.title: Link previews
changes.text: Every page now shows a title, summary and image with its headline number when a link is shared in a text, email or social post.

changes.title: Send a correction from the site
changes.text: A contact form on the About page sends corrections, records and questions straight to the BayCounty.me team. Email is optional and only used to reply.

changes.title: How they voted
changes.text: Recorded votes on budgets, tax rates, contracts, land and borrowing, with every member's vote and split votes first. Now covers the County Commission and every city: 351 votes, 115 of them split.

changes.title: Contracts and vendors
changes.text: Major contracts approved by Bay County and its cities since October 2022: winners, how they were awarded, change orders, emergency purchases, the bidding rules, and who the county actually paid the most.

changes.title: Fees, utility bills and who runs Bay County
changes.text: Every flat fee on Bay County tax bills, a typical monthly water, sewer and garbage bill in each city, and a guide to every elected seat, appointed manager and top salary. My Address now shows the actual fees on each parcel.

changes.title: Designed PDF reports, and a new home page
changes.text: Export PDF now builds a formatted report on every page, with tables, charts, maps and source links. The home page shows headline numbers and every topic.

changes.title: Debt and audit findings
changes.text: What every Bay County government owes, including big single payments ahead, and three years of audit findings in plain English, from audits filed with the Florida Auditor General.

changes.title: Search, and Hurricane Michael recovery money
changes.text: New: search across every page and record. New page tracking FEMA, HUD and state Hurricane Michael money in Bay County, with all 765 FEMA projects.

changes.title: My Address
changes.text: Look up any Bay County address for a tax estimate, representatives, schools, flood and evacuation zones, and CRA status. Uses the 2026 property roll.

changes.title: Amendment 3, and the homestead exemption fix
changes.text: New Amendment 3 page with the state's estimates for every Bay County government. Calculators now use the inflation-adjusted second homestead exemption ($25,722 for FY2026 bills).

changes.title: Tax dollars and the plain-English guide
changes.text: How your tax dollars are allocated: bill calculator, six years of rates and levies, and every government's budget. Plus a glossary and tap-to-explain terms across the site.

changes.title: CRA Spending launched
changes.text: Map and ledger of Bay County's six Community Redevelopment Agencies.

changes.title: Sort, filter and download every list
changes.text: Every table and list on the site can now be sorted by clicking a column heading, filtered with a search box (and drop-downs where a column has a few values), and downloaded as a CSV of exactly the rows on screen, in the order shown. Lists open newest first, then A to Z; upcoming meetings open soonest first.

changes.title: An API for BayCounty.me
changes.text: Every dataset on the site is now available through a free, read-only API with filtering, sorting and CSV output, plus an MCP server so AI assistants can look up and cite these records directly.

changes.title: Correction: Money map
changes.text: The first version of the Money map overstated connections. It counted a donor's contracts again for every official the donor gave to, which roughly doubled the government totals, and it drew lines from officials to governments they don't serve on. The map now puts each donor in the middle: campaign gifts on one side, the governments that pay the donor on the other, each counted once. It marks only gifts to an official whose own government pays that donor, and lists the recorded votes those officials cast on that donor's contracts. The heat map that credited contract dollars to individual officials was removed.

changes.title: Property tax exemptions, and exemptions on My Address
changes.text: A new page shows every property tax exemption in the 2026 tax roll, from homestead to disabled veterans, with how many homes get each and how much tax it takes off bills. My Address now lists each exemption on a home by name and uses the certified school and non-school taxable values, which corrects estimates for fully exempt homes and for seniors with the county senior exemption.

changes.title: Money map
changes.text: An interactive map of which businesses and groups gave to which officials, and where those same donors hold contracts with a local government, plus heat maps of giving by government and of contract dollars held by each official's donors.

changes.title: Budget explorer
changes.text: Open any government's FY2026 budget: spending by fund, General Fund spending by department, and revenue by source. Includes Callaway's and Parker's adopted budgets, which weren't on the site before.

changes.title: Every bond, note and loan
changes.text: The Debt page now lists each of 61 bond, note and loan issues with the amount borrowed, what is still owed, the rate, the final payment date and what it paid for.

changes.title: Compare governments side by side
changes.text: Pick any governments and compare budgets, tax rates, debt and staffing, in total or per resident.

changes.title: Upcoming public meetings
changes.text: Every board's next meetings, with agenda links and the money items on each agenda, checked daily. Add them all to your phone or computer calendar with one link.

changes.title: Campaign money and contracts
changes.text: The most recent campaign of each current elected official: how much they raised, from individuals and organizations, and which donors also hold contracts with local governments. Individual donors are counted, not named; each official's full report is linked.

changes.title: Request a public record
changes.text: Pick a government and a record this site is missing, or describe your own, and get a ready-to-send Florida public records request with the right office's contact details.

changes.title: Open data downloads
changes.text: Every dataset on the site, as CSV and JSON files you can open in a spreadsheet, with a description of each column.

changes.title: Zoning and development near your address
changes.text: My Address now shows the zoning and future land use at the address, development projects and orders within half a mile, recent rezonings, and conditional uses nearby.

changes.title: BayCounty.me en español
changes.text: My Address, the records request tool and the glossary are now available in Spanish. Mi dirección, solicitudes de registros y el glosario, en español.

changes.title: Address lookup understands more ways of typing an address
changes.text: My Address now finds addresses typed with full street types (Drive, Avenue, Boulevard), directions (North, West), highway forms (Hwy 98, US 98, County Road 2321), Saint or St., spelled-out numbers (Tenth Street), MLK, unit numbers, and a city, state and ZIP on the end. If a street type is wrong, it shows the closest matches.

changes.title: Clearer vote summaries
changes.text: Every recorded vote now has a plain-English headline and summary saying what was decided, rewritten from the motion in the minutes. The earlier text was pasted from the minutes and was often hard to read. Each card shows who voted which way and links to the minutes.

changes.title: Link previews
changes.text: Every page now shows a title, summary and image with its headline number when a link is shared in a text, email or social post.

changes.title: Send a correction from the site
changes.text: A contact form on the About page sends corrections, records and questions straight to the BayCounty.me team. Email is optional and only used to reply.

changes.title: Designed PDF reports, and a new home page
changes.text: Export PDF now builds a formatted report on every page, with tables, charts, maps and source links. The home page shows headline numbers and every topic.

changes.title: Tax dollars and the plain-English guide
changes.text: How your tax dollars are allocated: bill calculator, six years of rates and levies, and every government's budget. Plus a glossary and tap-to-explain terms across the site.
